admission.authority: direct user continuation of the divisor-layer lift experiment and opportunistic-shortcut policy
admission.reason: Extract the exact N-dependent fixed-gap multiplier hidden inside square divisors of N±1, and retain only the rare beyond-horizon power-of-two trigger as a low-cost opportunistic probe.

methods.name: BRC neighbor-square lift fixed-gap shortcut
triggers: large v2 of N plus or minus one
known square divisor of N plus or minus one
capabilities: derive m=2a-epsilon from any known a^2 dividing N-epsilon
reduce the multiplier-Fermat test to squarehood of mt+1 with fixed gap root abs(a-epsilon)
discover power-of-two square-divisor levels using v2(N±1) only
probe only multipliers beyond an existing bounded horizon
reuse the exact BALANCED quadratic-residue cascade before isqrt
recover a proper factor by gcd when the exact square witness splits N
return immediately to the ordinary exact fallback on a miss
methods.core_law: If N=a^2 t+epsilon with epsilon in {+1,-1} and m=2a-epsilon, then mN=a^2(mt+1)-(a-epsilon)^2. Therefore mt+1=c^2 gives mN=(ac)^2-(a-epsilon)^2. For a=2^k the trigger is read from v2(N-epsilon) with shifts only, making high-v2 multipliers beyond the ordinary scan horizon a very low-overhead free-option probe.
methods.hard_boundary: This is a specialization of classical multiplier-Fermat/difference-of-squares inside T0_BRC. Finite small-N diagnostics show very rare beyond-100 hits; it must not replace a complete scan, must not cause horizon expansion after a miss, and does not establish any asymptotic factorization improvement. Factoring N±1 merely to manufacture square-divisor metadata is outside the shortcut budget.
